item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: Today’s ‘Five Things’ leads with President Tinubu’s new foreign borrowing request, a six-month transport allowance for federal workers, an updated death toll from the Taraba killings, INEC’s investigation into suspicious photographs in the voters’ register, and the findings of the inquiry into deaths in NSCDC custody. 1. Tinubu seeks approval for $20.5 billion and €1.05 billion in fresh foreign loans President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve approximately $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external borrowing under the Federal Government’s 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. The request was presented to the Senate on Tuesday, 27 October. The President says the financing will support infrastructure, power, transport, healthcare, agriculture, education and employment-related projects across the country. Senate President Godswill Akpabio referred the request to the relevant committees, directing them to report within one week. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has urged lawmakers to withhold approval pending greater disclosure of project details. The borrowing has not yet been approved. Why it matters: The proposed borrowing is substantial and could have long-term implications for Nigeria’s debt obligations, public finances and infrastructure investment. Watch: The Senate committee’s findings, project-by-project disclosures, loan terms and the Debt Management Office’s assessment of repayment obligations. 2. Federal Government approves ₦70,000 monthly transport support for workers A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress reached several agreements during Tuesday’s negotiations in Abuja, easing immediate tensions over threatened industrial action. The government approved a ₦70,000 monthly transport intervention for federal public service workers across all grade levels, beginning in November 2026 and lasting six months. It also agreed to pay outstanding peculiar-allowance arrears in three monthly instalments and settle 19 months of outstanding health workers’ allowances over three months, beginning in December. However, the parties did not reach agreement on the effective date for a revised national minimum wage. They agreed to establish a negotiation committee and review implementation after one month. Why it matters: The intervention could provide temporary relief to federal workers facing high transport and living costs. It is not a permanent wage increase. Watch: Publication of payment guidelines, evidence that November disbursements begin as promised, the new wage committee and organised labour’s formal response to unresolved demands. 3. item.title: Violence Mars Gov Radda’s Funtua Campaign Flag-off As Supporters Report Injuries, Property Losses
item.description: Violence erupted along the route to the Tinubu–Dikko campaign flag-off in Funtua Zone on Wednesday, leaving several supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) injured and their property destroyed. The victims, who said they were travelling in the convoy of Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Radda, alleged that they were attacked by groups of angry youths and hoodlums while heading to the campaign venue, where the Governor was scheduled to present his administration’s Building Your Future scorecard. Some of the affected supporters told reporters that mobile phones, clothing and other personal belongings were destroyed during the incident, while several people sustained varying degrees of injuries. According to the victims, the attackers, whom they described as armed with machetes, knives, stones and bottles, assaulted them without provocation. “We were simply on our way to attend the campaign flag-off when we encountered some angry youths who attacked us with stones and bottles. Many people were injured, and our property was destroyed. We cannot afford to replace what we lost,” one of the victims said. The victims appealed to security agencies and relevant authorities to investigate the incident and bring those responsible to justice. Earlier, at the Malumfashi town roundabout linking Bakori Local Government Area, stones were seen scattered across the road, while several vehicles reportedly had their windscreens damaged, suggesting earlier disturbances in the area. Despite the disruption, Governor Radda proceeded with the presentation of his administration’s Building Your Future scorecard, highlighting achievements recorded since assuming office and outlining ongoing projects across key sectors ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The statewide campaign is designed to deepen grassroots engagement by taking the administration’s performance and development agenda directly to communities across the three senatorial zones of Funtua, Daura and Katsina, covering all 34 Local Government Areas and 361 wards. Authorities had not issued an official statement on the reported attack at the time of filing this report. item.title: NELFUND moves to stop students collecting loans while parents pay fees
item.description: …plans nationwide for re-education of students, institutions …400,000 students covered by the payment system pilot By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) has announced plans to clamp down on alleged double-dipping by students who benefit from its loan scheme while still relying on their parents to pay their school fees. The move, which signals a fresh effort to tighten accountability in the implementation of the Federal Government’s student loan programme, will also see parents provided with a mechanism to verify whether their children’s tuition fees have been paid through the scheme. Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, disclosed this on Wednesday during a press briefing, where he said the fund had identified cases of students allegedly accessing loan support while continuing to place the burden of tuition payments on their parents. Describing the practice as unacceptable, Sawyerr said the fund was determined to end the situation and strengthen transparency in the administration of the scheme. “This comment is based on our recognition that there are so many students out there who are double-dipping. They are taking from the NELFUND and still stressing their parents,” he said. “We are going to put an end to that.” Under the proposed arrangement, parents would be able to confirm whether their children’s school fees had been paid through NELFUND without necessarily having access to the actual amount involved. Sawyerr said the initiative was intended to address concerns among parents who continued to shoulder the financial responsibilities of their children’s education despite the availability of government-backed loans. The development comes as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to expand access to tertiary education through the student loan programme, designed to ease financial barriers and prevent eligible students from being denied higher education because of their inability to pay institutional fees upfront. Under the arrangement, NELFUND provides loans for institutional charges, while upkeep allowances are processed separately to assist beneficiaries with their living expenses. However, the fund’s latest intervention suggests that ensuring students understand the payment process, alongside preventing potential abuse, has become a priority as the scheme expands. To address gaps in understanding and clarify the revised procedures, NELFUND will organise re-education workshops across the six geopolitical zones of the country. Sawyerr explained that the exercise would go beyond the fund’s routine public awareness campaigns, which primarily inform students about the availability of the loan scheme. According to him, the new engagements would focus on educating students, parents and tertiary institutions on how the payment system works and the changes introduced to improve its administration. “We can easily do a press release and say, ‘Hey, this is what we’re doing.’ But if we don’t educate the institut

item.title: 22 Financial institutions yet to begin data localisation — NITDA survey
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Twenty-two of 44 financial institutions surveyed are yet to begin implementing measures to comply with Nigeria’s data localisation requirements, with the January 1, 2027 deadline approaching. The findings were presented by Dr Muhammad Aminu Lawal, Special Assistant on Digital Transformation to the Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, at the Executive Regulatory Dialogue on National Cloud and Software Infrastructure (NSCI) Implementation and Data Localisation in Lagos. The dialogue, convened by NITDA and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), brought together regulators, financial sector executives, banks, fintech operators and technology service providers. According to the survey, 26 institutions, representing 59 per cent of respondents, had completed the required actions or expected to complete them by the deadline. Fifteen said they were unlikely or very unlikely to finish on time, while three could not assess their readiness. The presentation summarised the findings by stating that “half are still planning; 22 of 44 have not started implementing.” It classified 59 per cent of the institutions as “on track” and 34 per cent as “at risk”. However, the presentation clarified that the responses were self-reported, anonymised and aggregated, stressing that they did not constitute a formal compliance assessment. The survey also showed that institutions had made more progress in identifying the data and systems covered by the requirements than in securing funding, engaging local providers or migrating systems. While 70 per cent had identified data or systems within the scope of the requirements, 52 per cent had mapped their hosting and administration arrangements. In contrast, only 25 per cent had secured board or executive approval and a budget, 23 per cent had contracted local providers, while 18 per cent had begun migration or remediation. “Mapping is done; budgets, contracts and migration lag,” Lawal said. Uncertainty surrounding the requirements was also identified as a major obstacle to implementation. The survey found that 64 per cent of institutions wanted a definition of “payment transaction data”, while 38 per cent sought clarification on what it means for data to be “stored and managed in Nigeria”. Twenty-nine institutions said they depended on further clarification to proceed with their preparations. The presentation identified a written clarification on the scope of the requirements as a priority, alongside clearer transition milestones, an exceptions process and guidance on existing contracts. It further showed that half of the institutions were proceeding on working assumptions while awaiting clarification, while 16 per cent said material work had been put on hold. item.title: Barcelona fined €602 over approach for Atlético Madrid’s Álvarez
item.description: Barcelona have been fined €602 by the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) following a complaint by Atlético Madrid over the Catalan club’s approach for Argentine striker Julián Álvarez. The sanction followed Atlético’s allegation that Barcelona contacted the forward, who remains under contract with the Madrid club until June 2030, without first notifying them in writing of their intention to negotiate a transfer. According to Reuters, the RFEF imposed the fine under Article 133 of its regulations, which covers minor breaches of regulatory obligations. Atlético had lodged complaints with both the Spanish federation and FIFA over Barcelona’s alleged approach. However, FIFA declined to consider the case, stating that it lacked jurisdiction. The disciplinary proceedings established that a conversation took place between Álvarez’s agent, Fernando Hidalgo, and Barcelona sporting director Deco on May 15, 2026, before Atlético received written communication on May 28. During the conversation, Hidalgo reportedly told Deco that Atlético would consider offers for the striker and indicated that he had permission to discuss a potential departure. However, the disciplinary committee said it could not establish that Atlético had authorised the agent to negotiate the player’s exit. The federation ultimately classified Barcelona’s conduct as a minor infringement rather than a serious offence, resulting in the €602 penalty. The club can appeal the decision. Álvarez’s potential move to Barcelona generated considerable tension between the two Spanish clubs during the summer transfer window after the Argentine expressed his desire to play for the Catalan side. The 26-year-old, who joined Atlético from Manchester City in 2024, has a contract running until 2030 and a reported release clause of €500m. His comments about wanting to fulfil his ambition of playing for Barcelona angered sections of Atlético’s supporters, who frequently booed him during matches this season. However, the striker recently sought to repair his relationship with the club’s fans after scoring the winning goal against Deportivo La Coruña on Saturday, his second consecutive match with a goal. Following the victory, Álvarez acknowledged that his earlier comments had upset supporters. “It was a mistake. I understand why the fans are angry. If I were a fan, I’d be angry too. Especially given how they’ve supported me since I arrived,” he said. The victory moved Atlético to within two points of LaLiga leaders Barcelona, while the reception Álvarez received after scoring suggested that relations with sections of the club’s supporters could be improving. Despite the controversy surrounding his future, Álvarez remains an Atlético player, with Barcelona’s pursuit ending in a financial penalty rather than a transfer. item.title: Nwoko: Okonjo-Iweala’s mother was women’s rights champion
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Chairman of the Senate Committee on Reparations and Repatriation, Senator Ned Nwoko (APC, Delta North), has commiserated with the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, over the death of her mother, Professor Kamene Okonjo. In a condolence statement he personally signed, Nwoko described the deceased as a distinguished scholar, renowned sociologist and committed advocate for women’s rights and empowerment. He said her life was marked by intellectual excellence, compassion, service to humanity and an enduring commitment to the advancement of women and society. Nwoko said: “Professor Kamene Okonjo was a distinguished scholar, a renowned sociologist and a committed advocate for women’s rights and empowerment. Her remarkable life was defined by intellectual excellence, compassion, service to humanity and an enduring commitment to the advancement of women and society.” The senator, on behalf of his family and the people of Delta North Senatorial District, extended his condolences to Okonjo-Iweala, the Obi of Ogwashi-Uku, Obi Ifechukwude Anishi Okonjo II, and the entire Okonjo family. He described the late professor as the matriarch of the Okonjo royal family of Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, who died at the age of 96. Nwoko noted that as the wife of the late Obi Professor Chukwuka Okonjo and mother of prominent individuals whose contributions had earned recognition locally and internationally, she left a legacy that transcended her immediate family. He said her contributions to scholarship, family life and women’s empowerment would remain a lasting part of her impact on society. “While her passing represents a profound loss to Ogwashi-Uku Kingdom, the Anioma nation and Nigeria as a whole, we must also celebrate a life of distinction, purpose and meaningful impact,” he said. The senator added that the values she upheld and the generations she inspired would continue to bear testimony to a life well lived. Extending his condolences particularly to Okonjo-Iweala, Nwoko said public achievements and positions could not diminish the pain of losing a mother. He prayed for God to grant the WTO chief, the Obi of Ogwashi-Uku, the Okonjo family and others mourning the deceased the strength and fortitude to bear the loss. He also prayed for the peaceful repose of the late professor’s soul, expressing hope that her legacy would continue to inspire generations. item.title: APC chair attacks Atiku over lack of projects in Plateau as VP
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has challenged former vice-president Atiku Abubakar to name one major project worth N10bn executed in Plateau State during his eight years in office. Yilwatda spoke on Wednesday at the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Jos, the Plateau State capital, while canvassing support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. “Atiku was vice president for eight years. Show me one road or one thing that we had on the Plateau. Show me one N10 billion project on the Plateau within that period,” he said. “The best we can have in those days is a borehole, or they bring ‘Keke Napep’ for us. Today, the president is bringing major projects on the Plateau,” he added. Yilwatda listed a univeristy and the Federal Medical Centre among projects associated with Tinubu’s administration, adding that the president had addressed challenges in healthcare, education, infrastructure and security. He identified insecurity as the most pressing concern among Plateau residents and credited Tinubu with addressing the problem. “If you ask any Plateau man, ‘What is your problem?’ The number one problem is insecurity, and Mr President has addressed it,” Yilwatda said. Also speaking at the event, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang urged residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the president should be allowed to complete an eight-year tenure in line with the North-South power-sharing arrangement. “There’s no reason why we will change the power-sharing formula between the north and the south; we’ve agreed that the south can do eight years and the north will do eight years,” he said. “President Buhari did eight years for the north there; there is no reason why the south cannot do eight years. He added, “We must be promise keepers; therefore, we have every reason to stick with the president.” The governor urged Nigerians to exercise patience and allow Tinubu’s economic policies time to produce results, describing the president as a “good driver” and arguing that there was no need for a change in leadership. item.title: The Signal: The Parties Are Choosing Sides. Will the Voters Follow?
item.description: Tinubu’s political alliances are expanding, Obi and Kwankwaso are sharpening their challenge, and INEC is under pressure to demonstrate transparency. But as the presidential campaign gathers momentum, Nigeria’s politicians may be discovering that winning endorsements is easier than winning public confidence. There is an interesting contradiction emerging in Nigerian politics. At a time when political parties are supposed to be competing against one another, their leading figures are increasingly finding reasons to work together. In Rivers State, Nyesom Wike is assembling a coalition that crosses party boundaries but supports President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. In Osun, Governor Ademola Adeleke supports Tinubu’s re-election while insisting that his political organisation will compete against the APC in legislative elections. Meanwhile, Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have established a joint presidential campaign structure, even as other opposition leaders continue discussing the possibility of a broader alliance. And the Independent National Electoral Commission, caught in the middle of growing political suspicion, has taken a step towards addressing concerns about the voters’ register. Welcome to Nigeria’s 2027 election. A contest in which party labels are becoming increasingly flexible, political loyalties are being renegotiated, and the electorate is being asked to distinguish between genuine conviction and political convenience. But beneath the manoeuvring lies a question that could determine the outcome. The politicians are choosing sides. Will the voters follow them? Wike’s coalition: when political boundaries become optional Nyesom Wike has never been a politician easily constrained by conventional party loyalties. His support for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, despite his association with the PDP, demonstrated his willingness to pursue political objectives across party lines. Now, with another presidential election approaching, he is taking that approach further. At a political gathering in Eleme, Rivers State, Wike made it clear that his Rainbow Coalition is not simply an arrangement to support Tinubu’s re-election. It also intends to support APC candidates contesting governorship and legislative elections. That is a significant development. It suggests that Wike is attempting to create a political structure capable of influencing elections at several levels, regardless of the formal party affiliations of those participating. There is a certain political logic to the arrangement. For Tinubu, Wike provides an influential ally in a strategically important state. For Wike, cooperation with the President offers a means of preserving political relevance and strengthening his position in Rivers. But what does the arrangement offer ordinary voters? item.title: South-East: Abia records 460,011 new voters, only 21,528 collect PVCs
item.description: By Steve Oko, Anayo Okoli, Emmanuel Iheaka, Vincent Ujumadu, Jeff Agbodo and Chinedu Adonu With preparations for the 2027 general elections gathering momentum, the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) has emerged as a major concern in the South-East, where the region accounts for the lowest share of Nigeria’s registered voters. While the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has reported progress in some states, the absence of updated figures in others has made it difficult to assess the overall level of PVC collection across the geopolitical zone. INEC statistics show that the South-East has 11,976,218 registered voters, representing 11.58 per cent of Nigeria’s national voter register of 103,428,715. The North-West leads with 25,083,411 registered voters, representing 24.25 per cent, followed by the South-West with 19,614,274, or 18.96 per cent. The North-Central has 16,965,787 registered voters, representing 16.41 per cent, while the South-South accounts for 15,823,550, or 15.30 per cent. The North-East has 13,965,475 registered voters, representing 13.51 per cent. The figures underscore the disparity in voter registration across the six geopolitical zones and the need for increased mobilisation in the South-East ahead of the 2027 elections. Investigations by Vanguard indicate that PVC distribution and collection in the region remain uneven, with some state offices yet to release updated statistics. Abia: Only 21,528 of 460,011 new registrants collect PVCs Only 21,528 of the additional voters registered in Abia State have collected their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the 2027 general elections, INEC has said. The figure represents about 4.7 per cent of the 460,011 additional registrants, raising concerns about the pace of collection as preparations for the elections intensify. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Abia State, Professor Sylvia Agu, told Vanguard that the state had 2,620,151 registered voters for the 2027 elections, compared with 2,180,140 in 2023. The difference between the two figures represents an increase of 440,011 registered voters. Agu said 21,528 PVCs had been collected as of October 22, 2026, explaining that the cards had not all arrived in the state, as INEC was receiving them in batches. She said the commission expected more PVCs to arrive and commended newly registered voters for their enthusiasm in collecting their cards. The REC added that INEC had been sensitising residents on the importance of PVC collection and expressed optimism that the exercise would record significant success in the state. Imo, Ebonyi yet to release updated figures In Imo State, INEC is yet to release certified figures for registered voters and PVC collection as it continues to address issues arising from the display of the voters’ register. item.title: Senate confirms Eze Anaba, 15 others to NHRC board
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has confirmed the appointment of the President of the Nigeria Guild of Editors (NGE) and Editor of Vanguard Newspapers, Eze Anaba, and 15 other nominees to the governing board of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC). The confirmation followed the consideration of a report presented on Wednesday by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (SAN, APC, Ondo Central). The Senate also confirmed Dr Salamatu Hussaina Suleiman as chairman of the board and Dr Anthony Ojukwu (SAN) as Executive Secretary. Other confirmed nominees are Mrs Roseline Tasha, Ambassador Adam Yubak Baku, ACG Felix Lawrence, Edmund Chinonye, Chinonye Obiaku (SAN), Oluwakemi Asiwaju Okere-Odo, Professor Adedeji Ogunji, Kingsley Chidozie, Mohammed Adelodu, Maupe Ogun Yusuf, Otunba Francis Meshioye, Patience Patrick Udoh and Hawwa Ibrahim. President Bola Tinubu had in April written to the Senate, seeking the screening and confirmation of the nominees as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s human rights protection framework. The letter was read on the floor of the Senate by the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. In the letter, Tinubu sought the reconstitution of the commission’s governing board in line with statutory provisions. The President said the nominations were made pursuant to Section 2(3) of the National Human Rights Commission (Establishment) Act, 2010, which empowers him to constitute the board, subject to Senate confirmation. The nominees were drawn from diverse professional backgrounds, including the media and legal sectors. The NHRC is mandated to promote and protect human rights, investigate alleged violations and encourage compliance with national and international human rights standards. The reconstitution of the board is expected to strengthen the commission’s institutional capacity to discharge its statutory responsibilities. item.title: Senate confirms seven FRC board nominees
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has confirmed the appointment of seven nominees to the board of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), including Dr Abdullahi Saidu as chairman. The confirmation followed the consideration of a report presented on Wednesday by the Vice Chairman of the Senate Committee on Finance, Senator Kamarudeen Olalere (Osun West). The confirmed nominees are Saidu as chairman, alongside Mohammed Asmau, Mohammed Makama, Suleiman Gidado, Louis Ndukwe, Amaechi Ugwele and Olaniyi Onikola as members of the commission’s board. President Bola Tinubu had last month written to the Senate, seeking the screening and confirmation of the nominees for appointment to key government institutions. The letter was read on the floor of the Senate on Tuesday by the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. Following the reading of the letter, Akpabio referred the nominations to the Senate Committee on Finance and directed it to report back within two weeks for legislative consideration. item.title: Indonesian Court Jails 11 For Abusing Toddlers At Daycare Centre
item.description: An Indonesian court sentenced 11 childcare workers on Wednesday to up to three years in prison for abusing toddlers at a daycare centre in a case that sparked nationwide outrage. Police had arrested the workers, all women, in April along with the principal of the facility and the head of the foundation that ran it. The arrests came after CCTV footage circulating on social media showed children, most under the age of two, lying on the floor wearing only nappies, their hands and feet bound with rags. Some of the children’s mothers wiped away tears as Judge Sunaryanto handed down each sentence, ranging from two to three years, at a court in Yogyakarta on Java island. The workers were “lawfully and convincingly proven to have committed the criminal offence of participating in placing a child in a situation of abuse and neglect, as well as participating in acts of violence against a child, carried out on an ongoing basis,” said the judge who, like many Indonesians, has one name. Imedia Dwi Anjani, whose four-year-old son was a pupil at the daycare, wept as she told AFP afterwards: “These children need a lot of therapy, so if the perpetrators are only sentenced to 2 years or 2.6 years, in our view as parents, that’s not fair.” Mothers of child victims react while attending the verdict sentencing session of daycare workers accused of child abuse and neglect at the Little Aresha Daycare, inside the Yogyakarta District Court in Yogyakarta on October 28, 2026. The footage of conditions at the facility triggered a public scandal, and the centre was closed soon afterwards. Police later said they had found 20 children crammed into a room just three metres (10 feet) long by three metres wide. They estimated that more than half of the about 100 children at the daycare were maltreated. City police chief Eva Guna Pandia said at the time that the women had told police they tied up some of the children to prevent them from disturbing others. They also said the centre was understaffed, with not enough personnel to bathe and dress the children. Parent Noorman Windarto told AFP in April his son was tied up and repeatedly hospitalised with pneumonia during his time at the centre, while his daughter sometimes came home with bruises her handlers said she must have sustained elsewhere. The principal and foundation head will be judged at a later date. AFP The post Indonesian Court Jails 11 For Abusing Toddlers At Daycare Centre appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Four Killed, 16 Injured In Lagos Road Accident
item.description: Four people have been reported killed, while 16 others were injured in an accident on Alaro City Bridge after a truck carrying a container overturned on a passenger bus at Berger Bridge, inward Eleko, along the Ibeju-Lekki Expressway in Lagos. The accident occurred in the early hours of Wednesday, according to the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA). While providing further details, the Agency noted that the articulated truck conveying a 20-foot container with an unknown registration number and a Toyota Hiace with registration number GME-589 ZU collided due to overspeeding, with the truck ascending the bridge at high speed, losing control, and overturning onto the bus. According to the Permanent Secretary of LASEMA, Dr. Olufemi Damilola Oke-Osanyintolu, they received a distress call regarding the fatal accident, and the ‘Beta Whales Team’ from Epe Base was deployed to the scene immediately. LASEMA also noted that the impact of the collision was severe. “The impact was severe and tragically resulted in the loss of four (4)adult males who were confirmed dead at the scene, while sixteen (16)other adult males sustained varying degrees of injuries. The Agency said the recovery operation is ongoing, and traffic management measures have been deployed to ensure safety. LASEMA towing truck involved in the accident Reacting to the development, the Lagos State Government commiserated with the families of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. Another truck accident was also reported around Vetland School, inward Agege Pen Cinema along Old Abeokuta Road at around 4:09 am, with the Tiger Team from C3 Base responding to the accident. The agency said the team observed a truck with registration number KTU-940XT which had rammed into a solar-powered streetlight pole before mounting the road median and obstructing vehicular movement as a result of reckless driving. According to the agency, they immediately implemented traffic diversion to prevent secondary incidents and to ease movement. “With the arrival of the Agency’s heavy-duty recovery equipment, Elephant, the affected truck was successfully recovered and conveyed to Abattoir Police Station for further investigation and safekeeping. The roadway has since been cleared and reopened for normal vehicular movement”. LASEMA also reported another accident at Igando along LASU-Igando road at Lanre Bus stop involving a DAF Truck with registration number SMK 795 XY which collided with a Toyota Corolla with registration number AKD 169 EA. They said, “Information gathered at the scene indicated that while a broken-down truck on the other side of the road had caused traffic build-up, the DAF Truck driving against traffic collided with the Corolla, blocking half of the road inward to Igando”. item.title: Nigeria would be rich if leaders left public funds in banks – Obi
item.description: Former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi has said Nigeria would be significantly wealthier if leaders left public funds in banks to generate interest instead of mismanaging the country’s resources. Obi, who is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the 2027 general elections, made the statement during an interview with a radio station in Nasarawa State on Wednesday, where he spoke about his administration’s approach to public spending, accountability and his record in basic education. The former Labour Party presidential candidate argued that the country could have accumulated substantial wealth if public office holders consistently protected government funds and allowed them to earn interest in financial institutions. “I wish everybody in this country left money in the bank; they have interest. Nigeria would have been so rich that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said. Obi disclosed that the funds under his administration were kept in three different banks, presenting the decision as an example of prudent management of public resources. He also lamented what he described as a culture of dishonesty and the tendency to discredit people who act with integrity in Nigeria. “Nigeria is a criminalised place. The criminals will always come together to show what the honest person did,” he said. The former governor further criticised what he described as a reversal of moral values, arguing that people who act honestly are often treated as though they have committed wrongdoing. “In Nigeria, to be honest is to be a criminal. To be criminal is to be honest,” Obi said. He added that Nigeria would have accumulated far greater wealth if its leaders had consistently left public funds in banks rather than diverting them. “We would have been worth so much that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said. Obi also addressed questions surrounding his administration’s public engagements, explaining that he believed the results of government projects should speak for themselves because they were financed with public funds. “We did what we were doing with public money, so the public already see us working, so why are we going to do the ceremony or showing it on TV? Maybe I was wrong, but that was what happened,” he said. The former governor also defended his record in basic education, insisting that Anambra performed exceptionally well in the sector during his tenure. “I was the best in education, basic education as a governor. You can go and check the records,” he said. He cited a visit by Professor Paul Collier of the University of Oxford, whom he said visited several states to assess developments in education and witnessed significant improvements. Obi maintained that education was a key measure of development and argued that his administration’s performance in the sector demonstrated the impact of responsible leadership. item.title: Real Madrid apologise to China over Mbappe comments
item.description: Real Madrid apologised to China on Wednesday for Kylian Mbappe’s comments poking fun at Mao Zedong, after the star striker’s remarks sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV. Mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo in China, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing. In a clip of a video interview with French show “The Bridge” — since taken down — Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao. Real Madrid “wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any offence caused by the recent remarks of our player Kylian Mbappe”, the club said in a statement. “The club joins in the public apology issued by Kylian Mbappe, in which the player himself expressed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people,” the 15-time European champions said. The statement came a day after Mbappe issued his own apology, in French, Chinese and English, saying: “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.” Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: “We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made.” La Liga, which saw the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said Tuesday it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans”. Earlier, the state-run Global Times said in an editorial that it was “not difficult to see that the club’s longstanding tolerance of such behavior has contributed to Mbappe’s latest offensive remarks”. Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground. CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of La Liga, the world’s second-richest football league after England’s Premier League. Mbappe, 27, continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist. “His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated,” wrote one user on social media platform Weibo. Mbappe’s original joke about Mao was not reposted — or had been scrubbed — from China’s tightly controlled social media. Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe’s account, where he has over a million followers. The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that “the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention”. item.title: Court dismisses Emeka Ike’s N10bn damages suit against Wike’s aide, INEC
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday dismissed N10 billion rights suit filed by the Nollywood actor Emeka Ike against Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant to FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Justice Salim Ibrahim, in a judgment, upheld the preliminary objections of the respondents on the grounds that the suit was incompetent and improperly constituted. Justice Ibrahim also dismissed the main suit on the ground of lack of proof. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Ike, who aspired to vie for the House of Representatives’ seat for AMAC/Bwari Federal Constituency, Abuja, for the 2027 general elections on the platform of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), lost the bid in a primary poll. The FCT minister’s aide, through a post on X in May, was alleged to have mocked Ike by leaking his confidential voter registration details on social media. The post was said to have shown details of Ike’s voter registration transfer from Imo to the nation’s capital. Meanwhile, Ike, in the suit filed by L. T. Adeh, sued Olayinka and INEC as 1st and 2nd respondents in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1272/2026. He asked the court to declare that Olayinka’s decision to publish his database on X without his approval “amounts to gross breach and violation of the applicant’s fundamental right to privacy and the protection of personal data”. Ike argued that Section 37 of the 1999 Constitution, Article 12 of the universal declaration of human rights, and Sections 24 & 39 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 guaranteed his right to privacy and protection of personal data. The actor asked the court to declare that INEC owes him and other voters a “statutory duty of care” to protect their private data against unauthorised access. The applicant, therefore, prayed the court to award him N10 billion against Olayinka and INEC as aggravated and general damages, to be paid jointly and severally for violating his fundamental right to privacy. He sought a declaration that the press release by INEC dated June 2, in reaction to the viral publication and circulation of his personal voter information and private data on social media by Olayinka, amounts to a tacit admission of guilt and liability to him. Ike, equally, sought an order directing Olayinka to immediately retract and pull down the offensive post and publication on his social media X handle, @OlayinkaLere, containing screenshots of his personal voter information and private data. He sought an order directing him to immediately tender an unravelling apology in writing for breach and violation of his fundamental right. But responding in a separate counter-affidavit, INEC and Olayinka prayed the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety. INEC, in its response, said the issue complained about in the suit filed by Ike was neither classified, sensitive nor confidential information. item.title: Thierry Henry explains Yamal joke after fans accuse him of disrespect
item.description: Former Arsenal and France striker Thierry Henry has explained his controversial remarks about Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal during the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, insisting that he had no intention of disrespecting the young footballer. Henry, who co-hosted the awards ceremony alongside Kate Scott on Monday, faced criticism after jokingly questioning whether Yamal really wanted the Kopa Trophy, an award presented to the best young player in world football. Yamal won the trophy for the third consecutive time, but Henry’s comments sparked reactions from fans who interpreted them as a suggestion that the teenager was overly concerned about winning individual honours. Responding to the backlash in a video shared on Instagram, Henry said his remarks had been misunderstood, stressing that he was a huge admirer of the Barcelona star. “For Lamine Yamal, I wasn’t checking his ego at all. I just thought that, as the third time that he’s winning that trophy, I just asked him if that’s the one that he really wanted,” he said. The former Barcelona forward explained that he had expected Yamal to compete for the main Ballon d’Or award, which was eventually won by England captain Harry Kane. “I am a big fan of Lamine Yamal. I wasn’t checking his ego whatsoever. That you didn’t like the joke, I can understand, but please don’t do that. He’s one of the players that I will pay to watch. I love him,” Henry added. He described Yamal as an exceptional talent whose performances he enjoys watching, expressing regret that the youngster did not claim the night’s biggest prize. “Unfortunately, he didn’t win it, because he’s a hell of a player that I enjoy to watch,” he said. Henry also addressed a separate controversy involving his co-host, Scott, after viewers criticised him for making a joke about her pronunciation of the name Socrates, the late Brazilian football legend. The former France international denied disrespecting Scott, maintaining that the exchange was planned and that she was aware of the joke before it was delivered. “Kate was with me on that joke,” Henry said. “And you can ask Kate, by the way. She did it on purpose, to say Socrates. And I had to say Socrates [with a different pronunciation].” He urged critics to stop portraying the exchange as an attempt to embarrass his colleague. “Again, that you didn’t like the joke, I understand. But please stop saying that I disrespect Kate. I will never do that,” he added. The 49-year-old further clarified his comments about Kane, explaining that although he supported fellow Frenchman Kylian Mbappe, he had congratulated the England striker on winning the Ballon d’Or. Henry said he praised Kane for his dedication and work ethic, describing the striker as a deserving winner. “I just said to him [Kane], ‘You are a worthy winner. You deserve it. item.title: Plane reportedly carrying Bolsonaro stops briefly in Ecuador
item.description: The plane that Argentine authorities say is carrying defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro made a brief stop in Ecuador on Wednesday, AFP journalists saw. Argentina’s government said Bolsonaro boarded a private flight operated by the company Baires Fly S.A. bound for the city of Guayaquil, Ecuador, with his wife and two daughters after arriving in Argentina on Tuesday night, despite a court order banning his exit. According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the Baires Fly flight took off just after midnight (0300 GMT) on Wednesday from the Argentine town of Puerto Iguazu in the country’s northeast. That flight landed in Guayaquil shortly before 4:00 a.m. (0900 GMT) before taking off again, AFP journalists and Flightradar24 data confirmed. Bolsonaro’s final destination is unknown, but the US State Department said it would issue visas to the senator and his family. item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: Tinubu seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with President Bola Tinubu writing to the Senate to seek approval for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects nationwide. Another headline reports that the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) agreed on a series of measures to ease the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and payment of 19 months’ arrears owed to health workers. Vanguard also reports that an independent ministerial committee recommended summary dismissal, administrative sanctions and prosecution of some officers of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) over the deaths of 33 detainees in the custody of its Niger State command in Minna, along with N1.4 billion in compensation for victims and survivors. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian leads with Nigeria’s mounting debt burden coming under heightened scrutiny as President Tinubu seeks legislative approval for fresh external loans of $21.7 billion ($20.52 billion and €1.045 billion), amid rising debt refinancing and little to no savings to liquidate maturing obligations. The Punch reports that Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara asked his supporters to stop referring to him as their leader, declaring that following his reconciliation with his predecessor, Nyesom Wike, he is now a member of the Rainbow Coalition, with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory as its leader. Lastly, Daily Trust reports that Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani declared his readiness to defend Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, insisting that his support for the president is based on conviction despite public discontent over economic hardship. item.title: Dangote Refinery’s IPO closes with investors from 120 countries
item.description: A Nigerian oil refinery owned by Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote has closed the continent’s biggest initial public share offering, claiming to have raised funds from investors in 120 countries. The IPO for the Lagos-based Dangote Petroleum Refinery was initially due to close on October 13 but was extended by two weeks to allow more Africans to participate. The company did not disclose how much money was potentially raised by the offering, after saying its target was $1.6 billion. But Aliko Dangote said earlier this month that it had exceeded that goal by “more than three, four times”. “This is a historic achievement for Africa. It shows what is possible when we believe in our continent, work together and invest in our shared future,” he said in a statement late Tuesday. The massive refinery has a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and aims to double its output to 1.4 million barrels per day, potentially making it the world’s largest refinery, surpassing the Jamnagar refinery in India. Investors from all 54 African countries and five other continents participated in the offering, the company said. “Investor applications spanning 120 countries demonstrate the extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence that investors are placing in the future of this refinery,” Aliko Dangote said “The opportunity to own a stake in a major African industrial enterprise has reached investors across every African country and all six inhabited continents,” he added. In July, the refinery secured $2.5 billion in investment from private investors. Last month, the company broke ground on a planned $16 billion refinery on Kenya’s Lamu island, with a projected capacity of 700,000 barrels a day. Africa currently imports more than 70 percent of its refined fuel, according to an Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) report in April. item.title: Four die; seven injured in Lagos accidents
item.description: Four persons died and seven others sustained injuries in three separate road accidents in Lagos on Wednesday, the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) has said. The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌⁠​​‍​​‌​agency said the fatal accident occurred at Berger Bridge, inward Eleko, along the Ibeju-Lekki Expressway, involving an articulated truck conveying a 20-foot container and an interstate Toyota Hiace bus. LASEMA’s Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, confirmed the incidents in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Wednesday in Lagos. Oke-Osanyintolu said the agency received a distress call and immediately activated its response team from Epe Base to the scene. According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that the truck was ascending the bridge at excessive speed when it collided with the bus. He said the truck driver lost control while attempting to avoid the collision, causing the truck to overturn onto the bus. Oke-Osanyintolu said four adult males died at the scene, while six other adult males sustained varying degrees of injuries. He said LASEMA, alongside the Federal Road Safety Corps and the Nigeria Police Force, secured the scene and administered first aid to the injured. He said the injured persons were subsequently conveyed to Epe General Hospital for further medical attention, he said. Oke-Osanyintolu added that a private crane had been secured to recover the overturned truck and container and facilitate the safe extrication of the deceased. He said the recovery operation was ongoing, with traffic management measures deployed to ensure safety along the corridor. In a related development, he said LASEMA’s Tiger Team from C3 Base responded to a truck accident at about 4:09 a.m. near Vetland School, inward Agege Pen Cinema, along Old Abeokuta Road. He said the truck, with registration number KTU-940XT, rammed into a solar-powered streetlight pole before mounting the road median and obstructing traffic. He said that preliminary findings attributed the incident to reckless driving, although no casualty was recorded. Oke-Osanyintolu said the agency deployed traffic diversion measures and later recovered the truck using its heavy-duty equipment, Elephant. He said the truck was conveyed to Abattoir Police Station for further investigation and safekeeping. He said the accident involved a DAF truck, with registration number SMK 795 XY, and a Toyota Corolla, with registration number AKD 169 EA. According to him, a broken-down truck on the opposite side of the road had caused traffic congestion when the DAF truck, allegedly driving against traffic, collided with the Corolla.
